title: When the Extraction Falls
premise: Dominic Halloran, a private security contractor who has learned to trust rules more than people, is assigned to protect a whistleblower courier carrying proof that a covert tri-national program is disappearing people — literally erasing them from records mid-flight. When the courier's plane vanishes from every radar and database, Dominic becomes the last person who remembers the passenger existed, hunted by an assassin who erases witnesses and by the three governments that funded the program. As she and a disgraced intelligence analyst, Theo Vance, race across Europe with the courier's hidden ledger, Dominic discovers the vanished flight carried her own missing brother, forcing her to choose between the duty that defined her and the truth that could destroy everyone she's sworn to protect. In the end she trades the ledger's original for a copy, exposing the program at a summit in Lisbon while the assassin — revealed to be a former colleague she loved — lets her live and disappears, leaving Dominic to rebuild a life from a memory no one else can verify.
about_author: Juniper Marchetti is the pen name of a former logistics coordinator who spent a decade moving sensitive cargo across borders before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about ordinary professionals trapped inside systems designed to make them forget.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A routine protection detail in Vienna establishes her meticulous, rule-bound world and her strained relationship with her employer, Meridian Protective Services. A small anomaly — a client's file that keeps rewriting itself — plants unease. Emotional beat: competent isolation, the ache of a life built on procedure instead of people.

chapters.title: The Passenger List
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. She's reassigned to shadow an unnamed courier, Ingrid Sorel, through Zurich. Ingrid is paranoid, brilliant, and carries a locked case she never puts down. Dominic notices a second watcher — a woman with a soldier's walk. Emotional beat: instinct firing against protocol; Dominic breaks a rule for the first time and photographs the watcher.

chapters.title: Vanishing Altitude
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Ingrid's flight to Prague drops off every tracker at 14,000 feet; no airline, no airport, no record admits it existed. Dominic's own assignment logs are scrubbed overnight. Emotional beat: vertigo — the ground truth of her profession dissolving beneath her.

chapters.title: Nobody Remembers But Me
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Colleagues deny the assignment ever happened; her handler calls her unstable. She finds one crumb: Ingrid's hotel receipt, and a name scrawled on it — T. Vance. Emotional beat: gaslit fury hardening into purpose; she goes off-grid.

chapters.title: The Analyst Who Burned
chapters.summary: Theo Vance's POV. A disgraced intelligence analyst in Lisbon recognizes Dominic's description of the vanished flight and lets her in — he's been tracking the same erasures for two years. He shows her the pattern: seventeen flights, forty-one people, all gone. Emotional beat: wary alliance; two lonely people recognizing the same wound.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Lost
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, with a flashback to Ingrid. Ingrid mailed a key to Theo before boarding; it opens a locker containing her ledger — names, routes, and the program's codename: EXTRACTION FALL. One entry stops Dominic cold: Halloran, M. Emotional beat: hope curdling — her brother may be among the disappeared.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Theo maps the program: a joint covert unit using record-erasure tech to disappear inconvenient people, funded covertly by three allied states. Dominic realizes her employer, Meridian, is the operational arm. Emotional beat: betrayal — the rules she worshipped were the weapon.

chapters.title: The Woman with a Soldier's Walk
chapters.summary: Assassin's POV (unnamed, 'Wren'). Wren is dispatched to retrieve the ledger and erase the last witness. We see her discipline, her handlers' contempt, and one flicker of hesitation when she sees Dominic's file photo. Emotional beat: cold professionalism with a hairline fracture.

chapters.title: Safehouse, Unsafe
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A Meridian safehouse in Lyon becomes a trap; Dominic and Theo escape through service tunnels as Wren closes in. Dominic recognizes Wren's movement patterns — they trained together years ago. Emotional beat: adrenaline and grief; the past is hunting her personally.

chapters.title: What Dominic Forgot
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, intercut with memory. A gap in her own history surfaces: a three-week blackout after her brother's 'accident' — an erasure she survived because she was inside the program's periphery. Emotional beat: horror turning inward; she may be evidence too.

chapters.title: The Berlin Broker
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. They seek a records broker who can decrypt the ledger's final layer; he names his price — the ledger itself. Negotiation, double-cross, and a narrow escape reveal the broker already sold their location. Emotional beat: trust tested; Theo lies to Dominic to protect her, and she catches him.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The alliance breaks: Dominic wants to go public immediately; Theo insists on verification, terrified of being erased mid-disclosure like his source was. They split the ledger's data. Emotional beat: love against duty in miniature — each choosing duty, each bleeding for it.

chapters.title: Wren's Ledger
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren recovers half the data but finds her own sister's name among the disappeared — a sister she was told died in a crash. She confronts her handler, who orders her to forget. Emotional beat: the assassin's fracture widens into a fault line.

chapters.title: Flight 447 Reversed
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Following the ledger's route data, Dominic reaches a decommissioned airfield in the Carpathians where the vanished planes were actually landed and passengers processed. She finds Michael's belongings — and proof he's alive in a facility. Emotional beat: grief overturned into ferocious hope.

chapters.title: The Facility
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Infiltration of the processing center: the disappeared are alive, memory-wiped, and re-issued new identities as deniable assets. Dominic finds Michael — and he doesn't know her. Emotional beat: the cruelest cost; rescue without reunion.

chapters.title: Extraction Falls
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Ordered to sanitize the facility before inspectors arrive, Wren instead finds Dominic and Michael. The confrontation is intimate — two women who once trusted each other with their lives, guns raised. Wren lowers hers. Emotional beat: love against duty, decided.

chapters.title: Running with Ghosts
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The escape across the border with Michael and Wren's evidence chip; Theo rejoins them, his verification complete. Wren's handlers mark her for termination. Emotional beat: a makeshift family of the erased, moving fast in the dark.

chapters.title: The Summit Gambit
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The plan: expose EXTRACTION FALL at the Lisbon security summit, where all three governments' ministers will share a stage. They have one window, one feed, and a traitor's warning that Meridian knows. Emotional beat: dread and resolve — the point of no return.

chapters.title: Lisbon, 09:14
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The climax: Meridian operatives breach the summit; Wren turns her skills against her former employers to buy ninety seconds; Theo broadcasts the ledger live. Dominic faces Meridian's director and chooses the truth over the quiet deal he offers. Emotional beat: everything staked, everything spent.

chapters.title: After the Noise
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The exposure detonates: inquiries, resignations, denials — and Michael's memory beginning to return in fragments, the first one her name. Wren vanishes before she can be arrested, leaving a single note: 'Some of us were taken too.' Emotional beat: exhausted tenderness.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Months later: testimony, a fractured Meridian, Michael slowly relearning his sister. Dominic declines a government offer to rebuild the same machine 'the right way.' Emotional beat: quiet reckoning — she chooses people over institutions, finally and completely.

chapters.title: The Woman on the Train
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, closing. On a Lisbon tram, Dominic spots Wren watching from the crowd — alive, free, unrepentant. Neither approaches; both smile. Dominic goes home to Michael and an ordinary evening she no longer takes for granted. Emotional beat: hard-won peace, with the door left open.
